state.task: Assess the browser-interface requirements of the canlang SaaS examples. The requested default belongs to the language: a left-hand sidebar that collapses, places the logo before automatically obtained page links, and anchors the account control below them. The account popover leads to a settings modal containing its own side navigation. Configuration of the current user's account must be a first-class facility with real validation and stored state. Authorization for the present pass covers only the 39 draft/Can*.md requirements documents; editing .can files, the parser, top-level language specifications or runtime implementation is outside this stage.
state.evidence: Separate staff, customer and public views occur throughout the drafts, which participate in 7 portfolio compositions. The existing localization contract covers messages in their owning source, translated page captions, standard runtime wording and a retained interface-language choice; there is still no running renderer. A global destination cannot use an unfilled record route such as /offers/{Revision.id} or /finance/invoice/{Invoice.id}. Non-parameterized destinations remain useful even below nested paths, including /tasks/my-work and /expenses/review. Existing team, company and record access rules, together with the canonical operations, continue to govern requests; showing or hiding navigation confers no permission.
state.shell: A selected deployment or composition receives a single common shell, combining identical selected page identities instead of putting a shell around each package. At its head sit the logo and app identity, followed by page links; at its foot sits the user/context control, with excess navigation height scrolling independently. On desktop, collapse retains accessible names for icons and an indication of the current destination; small screens use an overlay drawer that can be dismissed. Links generated by the shell obtain their route, translated title and availability from the page. Under the proposed default, accessible static navigation pages qualify, while detail routes needing parameters and auth/callback surfaces do not. Genuine declared navigation-placement differences could be supported later without repeating a menu declaration. Ordering, grouping and accessible links to parent views still need defined rules.
state.preferences: Provide account/security, language and appearance controls centrally through a runtime-owned primitive for the current user. Signed-in choices are retained under that principal within the applicable app scope; unauthenticated presentation choices stay in the browser. Where an app needs additional personal sections, those sections retain typed initial values and constraints and invoke the same canonical owner actions, avoiding an alternative implementation of business rules. Saving settings performs validation, keeps rejected input available, explains stale writes and allows resets where appropriate. Changing presentation leaves in-progress business forms intact and cannot alter grants, team/company authority, operational timezone, currency or recorded history. Changes to account identity/security follow the established authentication flows rather than unrestricted directory CRUD.
state.limits: Dedicated business-administration responsibilities are justified for six modules: Customer's company roles, Member's paid plans, Rent's published catalog and policies, Loyalty's reward program, Feedback's roadmap and moderation, and Trade's moderation. No additional administration console is needed for the remaining 33 modules. Developers continue to maintain technical credentials, endpoints, quotas, retention, retry behavior and report-source setup. Table and Reception currently prohibit settings areas in wording that must distinguish business/technical consoles from the shared personal-preference facility. The mention of a reception device does not authorize an anonymous kiosk.
state.risks: Obtaining meaningful destinations from page declarations reduces authored tokens, but depends on specified eligibility and order and on treating record-context gates correctly. Starting with all pages and removing unsuitable ones exposes each exception, with the cost of possibly recurring exclusions. An independently authored menu tree offers exact arrangement control, at the cost of repeating routes, labels and access facts contrary to the repetition objective. Central preferences avoid duplicating common schemas, while requiring a first-class ownership boundary and extensions with defined scope. Ordinary self-owned CRUD in each app reuses existing machinery, but repeats the baseline and makes account integration more complicated. These alternatives alone establish neither accessible interactions nor a feasible runtime.
state.research: The supplied primary sources are https://daisyui.com/components/drawer/ for markup supporting responsive and collapsible sidebars, plus https://daisyui.com/components/menu/ and https://daisyui.com/components/modal/ for component building blocks rather than finished application behavior. Modal keyboard and focus obligations are described by https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/. The distinction between disclosure navigation and application menus is covered by https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/. ADMIN_SURFACES.md already draws a boundary between shared/personal account controls and administration of the business. REQUIREMENTS.md continues to describe a Navbar shell, so this scoped revision must identify the sidebar as a future target rather than assert that current sources comply.
state.implementation: For this limited documentation stage, place the common target in CanDo.md and refer to it from the other app requirements. That arrangement neither makes app source/runtime depend on CanDo nor permanently relocates authority over the language. In every app document, specify its sidebar destinations, the page's components, content and actions, audience and detail-view treatment, only relevant personal settings, and frontend acceptance journeys. Retain all existing business constraints and identify later syntax/runtime alignment as unfinished. This work requires no extra requirements document, app-composition wrapper, general-purpose admin dashboard, component acquisition or verification framework.

navigation.instructions: Select the page-to-sidebar policy that most effectively satisfies destination usability together with the stated limits on source declarations and repetition.

criteria.eligible_pages: Generate destinations from accessible, non-parameterized navigation pages, categorically omitting detail/auth/callback surfaces and allowing declared placement exceptions; this requires eligibility and ordering rules.
criteria.all_then_exclude: Initially include all declared pages, then require explicit opt-outs for detail or otherwise unsuitable destinations; this makes exceptions apparent but may repeat exclusions.
criteria.menu_tree: Specify an independent navigation tree whose entries reference pages; this repeats arrangement information but gives authors direct control of placement.
criteria.unresolved: Leave navigation derivation undecided when none of the offered policies can satisfy the supplied constraints.

configuration.instructions: Choose the single base mechanism for first-class current-user settings that is compatible with the requirement to keep operations canonical.

criteria.runtime_primitive: Adopt a common runtime-owned current-user primitive, scoped typed personal additions and canonical save/authentication actions; this introduces a primitive and its state boundary.
criteria.per_app_crud: Represent each app's current-user choices with standard self-owned CRUD and generated settings interfaces; this repeats common schema definitions and requires separate account integration.
criteria.unresolved: Keep the base mechanism open if both proposals leave ownership, access or presentation separation unresolved.

coherence.instructions: Does the described sidebar and settings proposal, including this app-specific migration limited to requirements, remain consistent with public/customer/staff access boundaries, accessible modal interaction, canonical business operations and the restriction against unnecessary technical or administrative consoles?
